grounding.notes: All 5 snapshot-listed files spot-checked read-only against plan claims. Verified: api.py handler pattern is function(path_params, body) -> tuple[int, dict] (T03 implementation constraints match); queries.py exports exactly report_with_rows and reports_for_customer and its module docstring enforces the single-source rule (C2 constraint 'never read _REPORTS directly' matches repo intent); models.py is a plain dataclass module with fixture data c1:[r1,r2], c2:[r3] (T02's 'one page per report' and test fixtures r1/c1 exist); services/export.py is the only existing file under app/services/ (new-wiring rule for jobstore/pdf_export applies); tests/test_export.py asserts CSV shape and unknown-report KeyError (A5 'existing tests stay green' is concretely testable). README.md and TASK.md are in the snapshot's unknown_areas; the task requirements were checked against plan/input.md, which is the verbatim task record. No repo drift detected.

findings.evidence: stage-contract.json declares schema 'planning/stage-contract@2' but carries all five v1.1 governance fields (delivery_profile, planning_budget, horizons, stage_boundary, next_planning_trigger). Under the v1.1 contract closure a v1.1 workflow must emit planning/stage-contract@3; emitting @2 silently bypasses the @3 required-field enforcement. The bypass matters concretely: horizons.detailed_stage.tasks=[] and horizons.commitment.tasks=[] while the stage contains six tasks (T01-T06), and stage_boundary.stop_after=[] - the @3 schema requires stop_after with minItems 1, so a proper @3 contract would have failed schema validation and forced the horizon bookkeeping to be filled. As-is the governor has an empty commitment record to enforce against.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-emit stage-contract.json as planning/stage-contract@3: keep all content, set horizons.detailed_stage.tasks=[T01..T06], horizons.commitment.tasks to the certain subset, and stage_boundary.stop_after=[T06]. Local contract re-emission only - no DAG, package, or acceptance redesign. Eligible for TARGETED_PATCH despite POST_STAGE routing.

findings.evidence: run-manifest.json fails validation against run-manifest.schema.json (planning/run-manifest@1): 'plan-check.py validate' returns ok=false with six missing required keys (plan_id, stage_id, created_at, pipeline, gates, audit_verdict). The file instead uses ad-hoc keys (run_id, stages, final_lint, telemetry), and the on-file stage 7/8 entries claim 'validated: true'. plan-check lint does not validate this artifact, so the defect is invisible to the deterministic layer. It is a gate/attribution log, not an execution input, so it does not block execution.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite run-manifest.json to the run-manifest@1 shape: plan_id, stage_id, created_at, pipeline[] (stage/status/gate/artifact/exit_code per stage 0-8), gates[] (name/exit_code), audit_verdict, and carry the current stage/telemetry/final_lint content into notes.

findings.evidence: Frozen contract C2 specifies 'export_pdf(customer_id, report_id, lang) -> bytes' fetching via app/queries.report_with_rows (single report), but frozen_architecture decision DA-PDF-PER-REPORT states 'the PDF export service iterates over reports_for_customer(customer_id) and renders each'. These describe two different behaviors (per-report export vs whole-customer export). The inlined C2 spec is authoritative for T02 (it is the hashed frozen contract), and the per-report reading matches the endpoint shape POST /reports/{id}/export-pdf, so execution follows C2; the DA note is stale and could mislead T02's executor about which query to use.
findings.suggested_fix: Edit DA-PDF-PER-REPORT in stage-contract.json to 'export_pdf renders the single report named by report_id (one page) using report_with_rows' - or state explicitly that the endpoint exports one report per job. No contract spec change needed.

findings.evidence: T01's objective and deliverables require the worker to 'invoke PdfExportService' / 'call PdfExportService.export_pdf', i.e. implement the call against frozen contract C2, but T01.required_context.contracts lists only ['C1'] and T01.frozen_contracts inlines only C1. The C2 interface is referenced only as a paraphrase in allowed_dependencies ('worker calls export_pdf(customer_id, report_id, lang) -> bytes'); the full C2 spec - including 'Raises PdfExportError on failure' and lang ValueError semantics that T01's failure_cases depend on - is inlined only in T02's package.
findings.suggested_fix: Add C2 to T01.required_context.contracts and inline the full C2 spec (with source_hash) into T01.frozen_contracts so the T01 executor sees the authoritative error-type contract without reading T02's package.

findings.evidence: Stage acceptance A4 positive_case: 'Export with lang=de produces a PDF with German label text' does not name which label keys or which German strings a third party must assert. It is checkable at execution time because T02's deliverable (i18n module) defines the labels and AT06 pins the test (test_i18n_labels), but the stage-level criterion alone is not independently verifiable without reading T02's package.
findings.suggested_fix: Name the label keys (e.g. report title, period, metric columns) and the expected German strings in A4's positive_case, or reference AT06 explicitly as the evidence.

findings.evidence: plan-check lint reports 17 MINOR VAGUE_ACCEPTANCE findings across stage-contract.json and tasks/*.json: acceptance description fields lack inline pytest markers. The paired evidence fields DO carry concrete pytest references (e.g. tests/test_e2e_pdf.py::test_full_export_flow), so the acceptance is deterministic in substance; only the description style triggers the lint.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the pytest test reference to each flagged description field (or accept the 17 minors as style noise for alpha). Low priority - evidence fields are sufficient for execution and for the P5 scorer, which counts blockers only.

verdict_rationale: Zero BLOCKER findings; verdict is data for the governor, not a gate. The single deterministic blocker (AUDIT_NOT_ISOLATED) pointed at the replaced round-1 in-conversation audit file and is resolved by this isolated re-audit. Semantic pass: scope matches the task with all three task-level out-of-scope items plus two grounded extras (no email bait - email appears only as an out_of_scope entry and a T01 non-goal); non-goals are sufficient and reasoned; contracts C1/C2/C3 are frozen before the parallel group [T01,T02,T03] with hashed inlining in every consuming package; ownership paths are disjoint (jobstore/tests, pdf_export+i18n+shim/tests, api/tests, checkpoints, e2e test file); fake-serialization removals (T02->T01, T01->T03) are justified by frozen-contract test fakes; both seams S1/S2 are covered by a seam_integration task (T05) plus e2e_closure (T06) whose E2E gates include failure scenarios (404, 400, 409, job-failure); leaves are S-footprint with documented merge rationales; the pdflib_shim uncertainty is handled by making the shim a T02 deliverable (no spike needed for alpha); single stage with empty forecast, no over-planning. Findings: 1 MAJOR (contract emitted as @2 with empty v1.1 horizons - should have been @3; local re-emission fix) and 5 MINOR, all with concrete local fixes and none threatening a stage acceptance criterion.
